# Fixture: error_beyond_edges

A non-fatal error that silently drops a call in a header which no recorded
include edge connects to the failing unit (B-27, third review). The
analysis root is `root/`; `gen/` and `ext/` lie outside it.

- `root/h1.h` declares `g` with a parameter of the unknown type
  `undefined_t`: an error on line 8. `root/h2.h` defines `static int k(void)`,
  which calls `g`; Clang suppresses the follow-on error, so the call becomes
  an expression with errors and is not recorded (as in `recovery_expr`).
- `root/other.c` defines `g` and `other`, and parses cleanly.

Two compilation databases, generated by the test, each with `other.c`:

1. `../gen/main.c` (a generated main file outside the root) with `-I.`: it
   includes `h1.h` and `h2.h`. Its main file is not a recorded file and its
   directives are not recorded, so no edge reaches `h2.h`.
2. `main.c` with `-I. -I../ext`: it includes `h1.h` and `wrap.h`, which is
   found in `ext/` (outside the root) and includes `h2.h`. Directives of
   files outside the root are not recorded, so no edge reaches `h2.h`.

Expected facts in both: `k` is a definition in `h2.h` with no call edges,
and the analysis has an error diagnostic in `h1.h`. "`k` does not call
`g`" must not be confirmed.
